chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Country and Judge Gershon
summary: Country, chauffeur to Judge Gershon, helped musicians in trouble. She tells the story of Gershon hunting for him and his pawned Cadillac tyres.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh goodness, I've forgotten the street. I think 18th and Vine. This was where they had a floor show and everything but after the floor show everybody would jam I guess from 1 o'clock till maybe 12 the next day. We had a wonderful friend that used to help out the musicians. He and Piney Brown were really friends of the musicians. He was known by the name of Country and he worked for a judge there, Judge Gershon. We used to laugh about the two of them together. Country was the chauffeur and Judge Gershon's right-hand man. Whenever anybody got into trouble Country would - these two were the most comical act you've ever seen, whether in the movies or anything. Whenever one of the musicians had gotten into trouble his case

would come up in court and Gershon would say, "So-and-so blabla," whatever his name was and Country would sneak out the door. He'd say, "Come back here, Country. I know what you've done." See the musician didn't appear and Country had gone out to where he was jailed and told that Judge Gershon said to turn him loose. It was a big political town anyway and he did things like that and the Judge would come down 18th Street - I saw him myself. It happened to be around 3 o'clock and he'd look in all the pool halls and all the restaurants and everything, asking for Country and Country was hiding underneath the pool table. Country was a fabulous and fine-looking tall black man. He was just handsome. He was hiding under this pool table and Gershon was walking up and down 18th Street looking for him. He'd say, "Don't tell him where I am." He'd gotten drunk all night and had lost his voice and everything, so Gershon said, "I'm looking for Country. Do you know what he did?" Country had pawned two tires on his Cadillac. He'd carry on with the musicians and buy drinks and do things for them so this particular night he pawned these two tires and the car was hiked up on one side without any tires on it. That was really funny, what happened with him. Let's see, something else happened.
